key_insight: A DSL-guided multi-agent LLM system can improve inverse materials design by grounding natural-language design rules in symbolic predicates and statistical evidence.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a practical route to discover candidate perovskite oxides for target properties without requiring large task-specific training datasets or retraining.
method: Translate design rules from natural language into chemistry DSL predicates.
Use accumulated materials data to test, validate, and refine rules during iterative LLM-driven design.
Deploy a multi-agent framework (ORCHESTRA) for inverse design of double perovskite oxides under multiple objectives.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that symbolic predicates helped identify unsupported rules, validate new rules, and improve the rule store over iterative design cycles, with better performance than a natural-language-only strategy, especially for harder targets.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and completeness of the underlying materials data and the predefined DSL, which may limit generalization to unfamiliar chemistries.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
